reason: Non-tubular means not tubular.
Hyacinth-scented names a specific scent. Mapping it to sweet-scented loses that.
Not flaking means not exfoliating, usually said of bark.
Stomata-free means the stomata are absent.
A falsely racemose inflorescence only resembles a raceme, so raceme-like fits.
Seedy means containing seeds. It is read as seed present, and only in fruit contexts.
Bunchy means clustered. It matches caespitose (tufted) only for the habit of the whole plant or its shoots.
Not peeling means not exfoliating, usually said of bark.
Waited is almost certainly an OCR or typing error for waisted, and no other sense is plausible in a flora. A rule that fixes it is acceptable.
Whippy means flexible and slender, so flexible is a fair target.
A lacerate-margined part has a lacerate margin.
Coalescing parts are fused, which is the sense of connate.
Straplike means strap-shaped.
Mushy means soft, usually of fruit or tissue.
Articulating means having a joint, which is jointed.
Auricle-less means without auricles, so not auriculate.
Bland is a taste word. It applies only to parts that are tasted.
Cymulose means bearing cymules, a form of cyme. The PO cyme class lists cymule as a synonym.
Glassy usually means shiny or lustrous, or transparent. It does not reliably mean translucent, so the rule should be rejected.
Hirtello-puberulent combines short stiff hairs (hirtellous) with puberulent. Puberulous alone loses the stiff-hair part.
Incoherent means not coherent, as in not fused or not cohering.
The adverb narrowly is only a degree. The shape is clavate.
Not appressed is the negation of appressed.
Not leaflike is the negation of leaf-like.
Not oblique is the negation of oblique.
Not reflexing is read as not reflexed.
Not ridged is the negation of ridged.
Spinulose-aristate means minutely spiny and awned. Spine-tipped loses the awn (aristate) part.
Uncompressed means not flattened.
Widely ovate is ovate. The adverb only gives the degree.
A base gradually narrowed is tapered. The base is the part, and tapered is the quality.
Blade-bearing means having a lamina.
Broadly expanded means dilated.
Bulblet-bearing means having bulblets. The PO bulb class lists bulblet as a synonym.
Chalk white is white.
Clavulate is a diminutive of clavate, so it is clavate.
Coarsely reticulate is reticulate. The adverb only gives the degree.
Featherlike is plumose, and PATO lists feathery as a synonym.
Not cleft is the negation of cleft.
Not slender is the negation of slender.
Spinose means spiny, so not spinose is not spiny.
Remotely spaced means distant.
Shallowly saucer-shaped is saucer-shaped. The adverb only gives the degree.
Smudged means marked with smears or blotches, so blotchy is close enough.
Sparsely scattered means sparse.
Thyrselike means thyrse-like.
Bifarious means arranged in two rows, which is distichous.
Bulky means large in volume. Increased size is acceptable.
Callose-apiculate means a short point with a callose (hard, thickened) tip. Mucronate loses the callose part.
Carpellate means bearing carpels but no stamens, which is female. The bearer constraint is appropriate.
